Meg Ryan's Top 10 Movies Ranked

4 July 2023 · RewindZone Archive

From 90's Heart throb to "Whose that?"

Meg Ryan, the beloved actress known for her captivating performances, has starred in numerous films throughout her career. From romantic comedies to gripping dramas, Ryan's talent and on-screen presence have left a lasting impression on audiences. However, as the years went by, her choice of roles became increasingly repetitive and predictable, leading to a decline in both critical acclaim and box office success. Additionally, Ryan's notable absence from the spotlight and lack of significant projects in recent years has further contributed to her downfall. It is disheartening to witness the fading of a talent that once brought joy to audiences worldwide, leaving us to wonder what could have been if she had pursued more diverse and challenging roles (Other than In the Cut - uurgh!) In this article, we will explore Meg Ryan's top 10 movies, ranked based on our own rankings as well as IMDB scores. Join us on a journey through Ryan's most remarkable films that have contributed to her enduring legacy in the world of cinema.

You can find Our Meg Ryan List further down the page for more Info and Streaming choices

1. When Harry Met Sally... (1989)

Advertisement

IMDb Rating: 7.6/10

"When Harry Met Sally..." is a timeless romantic comedy that showcases Meg Ryan's impeccable comedic timing and on-screen chemistry with Billy Crystal. As Sally Albright, Ryan delivers a memorable performance, capturing the complexities of love and friendship with authenticity and charm. This film remains a beloved classic, and Ryan's portrayal of Sally continues to resonate with audiences of all generations.

2. Sleepless in Seattle (1993)

IMDb Rating: 6.8/10

In "Sleepless in Seattle," Meg Ryan shares the screen with Tom Hanks in a heartwarming tale of love and destiny. Ryan's portrayal of Annie Reed, a woman who falls in love with a widower through a radio talk show, captivates viewers with her endearing charm. This romantic comedy showcases Ryan's ability to bring depth and vulnerability to her characters, making it a fan-favorite in her filmography.

3. When a Man Loves a Woman (1994)

IMDb Rating: 6.5/10

"When a Man Loves a Woman" delves into the complexities of addiction and the impact it has on a marriage. Meg Ryan delivers a powerful performance as Alice Green, a woman struggling with alcoholism. Ryan's portrayal of Alice's journey through recovery and the strain it puts on her relationship showcases her ability to tackle emotionally charged roles with depth and authenticity. In our opinion, Meg Ryan's best dramatic role of her career.

4. You've Got Mail (1998)

IMDb Rating: 6.6/10

In "You've Got Mail," Meg Ryan reunites with Tom Hanks in a delightful romantic comedy set in the early days of internet communication. Ryan's portrayal of Kathleen Kelly, a small bookstore owner who unknowingly falls for her online business rival, showcases her unique blend of warmth and comedic timing. Her on-screen chemistry with Hanks once again shines through, making this film a beloved addition to Ryan's repertoire.

5. Courage Under Fire (1996)

Advertisement

IMDb Rating: 6.6/10

In "Courage Under Fire," Meg Ryan displays her dramatic range as Captain Karen Emma Walden, a helicopter pilot who becomes a posthumous candidate for the Medal of Honor. Ryan's portrayal of a strong and resilient military officer grappling with personal demons adds depth to this gripping war drama. Her performance stands as a testament to her ability to tackle complex and emotionally charged characters.

6. City of Angels (1998)

IMDb Rating: 6.7/10

"City of Angels" explores the themes of love, loss, and spirituality in a poignant romantic fantasy film. Meg Ryan portrays Dr. Maggie Rice, a heart surgeon who captures the attention and affection of an angel, played by Nicolas Cage. Ryan's performance beautifully conveys the complexities of love and the longing for human connection, adding depth to this thought-provoking story.

7. Addicted to Love (1997)

IMDb Rating: 6.1/10

"Addicted to Love" showcases Meg Ryan's comedic talents in this unconventional romantic comedy. Playing the role of Maggie, a jilted lover seeking revenge, Ryan injects the film with her unique blend of wit and charm. Her portrayal of Maggie's emotional journey highlights her ability to navigate complex characters with depth and authenticity.

8. Innerspace (1987)

IMDb Rating: 6.8/10

In the sci-fi comedy "Innerspace," Meg Ryan stars alongside Dennis Quaid in a thrilling adventure. Ryan's role as Lydia Maxwell, a journalist caught up in a scientific experiment gone awry, allows her to showcase her versatility as an actress. Her on-screen chemistry with Quaid and her ability to bring levity to the film's action-packed narrative make this an entertaining addition to Ryan's filmography.

9. French Kiss (1995)

IMDb Rating: 6.6/10

"French Kiss" sees Meg Ryan embarking on a romantic adventure in the picturesque landscapes of France. As Kate, a woman determined to win back her ex-fiancé, Ryan infuses the film with her trademark charm and comedic timing. Her portrayal of Kate's transformation and self-discovery offers a delightful blend of romance and comedy, making it an enjoyable watch.

10. Joe Versus the Volcano (1990)

IMDb Rating: 5.8/10

"Joe Versus the Volcano" presents a whimsical and offbeat story in which Meg Ryan plays three different characters opposite Tom Hanks. Ryan's versatility shines as she effortlessly portrays each distinct role, adding depth and quirkiness to this comedic tale of self-discovery and adventure.

Honourable Mentions

Conclusion

Meg Ryan's top 10 movies feature a diverse range of genres, showcasing her talent and versatility as an actress. From her iconic romantic comedies like "When Harry Met Sally..." and "Sleepless in Seattle" to her compelling performances in dramas like "When a Man Loves a Woman" and "Courage Under Fire," Ryan has definitely left her mark on the world of cinema. Her ability to embody relatable characters and evoke genuine emotions has endeared her to audiences around the globe. As we celebrate Meg Ryan's cinematic legacy, we eagerly anticipate the future roles and performances which can hopefully reinvigorate her career!

Note: The IMDb ratings mentioned in this article are accurate as of the time of writing and are subject to change over time.
